metadata.title: On the Distribution of the Length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence of Random Permutations

nodes.name: Longest increasing subsequence length $l_N$
nodes.statement: For $\pi \in S_N$, $l_N(\pi)$ denotes the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\pi$, i.e. the largest $k$ such that there exist $i_1 < \cdots < i_k$ with $\pi(i_1) < \cdots < \pi(i_k)$.

nodes.name: Distribution $q_{n,N}$
nodes.statement: Equip $S_N$ with uniform distribution. Then $q_{n,N} = \mathrm{Prob}(l_N \le n) = f_{N,n}/N!$, where $f_{N,n}$ is the number of permutations $\pi \in S_N$ with $l_N \le n$.

nodes.name: Painlevé II equation and Hastings-McLeod solution $u(x)$
nodes.statement: $u(x)$ is the (unique) solution of $u_{xx} = 2u^3 + xu$ with $u(x) \sim -\mathrm{Ai}(x)$ as $x \to +\infty$, where $\mathrm{Ai}$ is the Airy function.

nodes.name: Tracy-Widom distribution $F(t)$
nodes.statement: $F(t) = \exp\bigl(-\int_t^\infty (x-t) u^2(x)\,dx\bigr)$, where $u(x)$ is the Hastings-McLeod solution of PII.

nodes.name: Poissonization $\phi_n(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: $\phi_n(\lambda) \equiv \sum_{N=0}^{\infty} \frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^N}{N!} q_{n,N}$. Equivalently, the distribution function of $L(\lambda)$ from a rate-one planar Poisson process.

nodes.name: Toeplitz determinant representation $D_{n-1}$
nodes.statement: $\phi_n(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda} D_{n-1}(\exp(2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta))$, where $D_{n-1}$ is the $n \times n$ Toeplitz determinant with weight $f(e^{i\theta}) = \exp(2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta)$ on the unit circle.

nodes.name: Orthonormal polynomials $p_n(z;\lambda)$ on the unit circle
nodes.statement: $p_n(z;\lambda) = \kappa_n(\lambda) z^n + \cdots$ are the polynomials orthonormal with respect to $f(e^{i\theta})\frac{d\theta}{2\pi} = \exp(\sqrt{\lambda}(z+z^{-1}))\frac{dz}{2\pi i z}$ on $\Sigma$. Then $\kappa_n^2(\lambda) = D_{n-1}(\lambda)/D_n(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Riemann-Hilbert Problem (RHP) $(\Sigma,v)$
nodes.statement: Given an oriented curve $\Sigma$ and jump $v: \Sigma_0 \to GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, find $Y(z)$ analytic in $\mathbb{C} - \Sigma$ with $Y_+(z) = Y_-(z) v(z)$ on $\Sigma_0$ and $Y(z) \to I$ as $z \to \infty$.

nodes.name: RHP $(\Sigma_{\theta_0}^{PII}, v_x^{PII})$ for Painlevé II
nodes.statement: RHP on the rotated 6-ray contour $\Sigma_{\theta_0}^{PII}$ with jump $v_x^{PII}(z) = e^{-i\theta_{PII}\,\mathrm{ad}\,\sigma_3} v^{PII}$, $\theta_{PII} = \frac{4z^3}{3} + xz$ and singular monodromy data $p = -q = 1$, $r = 0$. The solution $m_{\theta_0}^{PII,1}$ encodes $u(x) = 2i\,m_{1,12}^{PII}(x)$.

nodes.name: RHP $(\Sigma^{PII,2}, v^{PII,2})$
nodes.statement: Equivalent deformed RHP for PII on a contour $\Sigma^{PII,2}$ consisting of a pair of curves in $\mathbb{C}_\pm$, with jump $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ in $\mathbb{C}_+$ and $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ in $\mathbb{C}_-$; equivalent to the original PII RHP.

nodes.name: RHP $(\Sigma^{PII,3}, v^{PII,3})$ with $g$-function
nodes.statement: For $x < 0$, the second equivalent PII RHP, conjugated by $e^{i(g^{PII}(z) - \theta_{PII}(z))\sigma_3}$ with $g^{PII}(z) = \frac{4}{3}(z^2 + x/2)^{3/2}$, on a 5-ray contour $\Sigma^{PII,3}$.

nodes.name: RHP $(\Sigma, v)$ for $\kappa_k^2(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be the unit circle. Find $Y(z;k+1,\lambda)$ analytic in $\mathbb{C} - \Sigma$ with $Y_+ = Y_- \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1 & z^{-(k+1)} e^{\sqrt{\lambda}(z+z^{-1})}\\0 & 1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on $\Sigma$, and $Y(z) z^{-(k+1)\sigma_3} = I + O(1/z)$ at $\infty$. Then $\kappa_k^2(\lambda) = -Y_{21}(0;k+1,\lambda)$.

nodes.name: $g$-function and equilibrium measure $d\mu_V$
nodes.statement: $g(z) = g_V(z) \equiv \int_\Sigma \log(z-s)\,d\mu_V(s)$, where $d\mu_V$ is the unique probability measure on $\Sigma$ minimizing $\iint \log|z-w|^{-1}\,d\mu(z)d\mu(w) + \int V(z)\,d\mu(z)$ for the external potential $V(z) = -\frac{\gamma}{2}(z + z^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Parameter $\gamma = 2\sqrt{\lambda}/(k+1)$
nodes.statement: $\gamma = \frac{2\sqrt{\lambda}}{q}$ with $q = k+1$. The support of $d\mu_V$ is the whole circle for $0 \le \gamma \le 1$ and develops a gap for $\gamma > 1$; $\gamma = 1$ is the third-order phase-transition point of Gross-Witten / Johansson.

nodes.name: Function $\alpha(z)$ on the gap regime
nodes.statement: $\alpha(z) = -\frac{\gamma}{4}\int_\xi^z \frac{s+1}{s^2}\sqrt{(s-\xi)(s-\xi^{-1})}\,ds$ with $\xi = e^{i\theta_c}$, branch analytic in $\mathbb{C} - \overline{C_1}$ and $\sqrt{(s-\xi)(s-\xi^{-1})} > 0$ for real $s > 0$.

nodes.name: Centered/scaled variable $\chi_N$
nodes.statement: $\chi_N \equiv (l_N - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6}$ is the centered, scaled length of the longest increasing subsequence in a uniform random permutation of $[N]$.

nodes.name: Convergence of $\chi_N$ to Tracy-Widom (Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let $\chi$ have distribution $F$. Then $\chi_N = (l_N - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6} \to \chi$ in distribution as $N \to \infty$, i.e. $\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathrm{Prob}(\chi_N \le t) = F(t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$.
assumptions: $l_N(\pi)$ is the longest increasing subsequence length
$F$ is the Tracy-Widom distribution from $u(x)$ solving PII

nodes.name: Convergence of moments (Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: For every $m = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$, $\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E}_N(\chi_N^m) = \mathbb{E}(\chi^m)$. In particular, $\lim_N \mathrm{Var}(l_N)/N^{1/3} = \int t^2 dF - (\int t\,dF)^2$ and $\lim_N (\mathbb{E}_N(l_N) - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6} = \int t\,dF$.
assumptions: Tail bounds $F_N(t) \le C(M)e^{ct^3}$ for $-2N^{1/3}\le t\le -M$ and $1-F_N(t) \le C(M)e^{-ct^{3/5}}$ for $M \le t \le N^{5/6}-2N^{1/3}$

nodes.name: Gessel/OPWW Toeplitz determinant identity
nodes.statement: $\sum_{N=0}^\infty \frac{\lambda^N F_N(n)}{N!} = \det(d_{j-k})_{0 \le j,k \le n-1}$, where $d_j = (2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi} e^{2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta - ij\theta}\,d\theta$. Equivalently $\phi_n(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda} D_{n-1}(\exp(2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta))$.
assumptions: $F_N(n) = N! q_{n,N}$ counts permutations with $l_N \le n$
$D_{n-1}$ is the Toeplitz determinant of weight $\exp(2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta)$

nodes.name: Tracy-Widom largest GUE eigenvalue distribution
nodes.statement: For the GUE of $N \times N$ Hermitian matrices, the suitably centered and scaled largest eigenvalue converges in distribution to the law $F(t) = \exp(-\int_t^\infty (x-t)u^2(x)\,dx)$ as $N \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Hastings-McLeod existence/uniqueness for PII
nodes.statement: There exists a unique global solution $u(x)$ of $u_{xx} = 2u^3 + xu$ with $u(x) \sim -\mathrm{Ai}(x)$ as $x \to +\infty$, with asymptotics $u(x) = -\sqrt{-x/2}(1 + O(1/x^2))$ as $x \to -\infty$.

nodes.name: Szegő strong limit theorem
nodes.statement: For Toeplitz determinants with weight $f(e^{i\theta}) = \exp(2\sqrt{\lambda}\cos\theta)$ on the unit circle, $\lim_{n \to \infty} D_n(\lambda) = e^\lambda$. Hence $\log\phi_n(\lambda) = \sum_{k=n}^\infty \log\kappa_k^2(\lambda)$.
assumptions: Smooth positive weight on the unit circle

nodes.name: Existence/uniqueness for RHP $Y$ (Lemma 4.1)
nodes.statement: The RHP for $Y(z)$ with jump $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1 & z^{-(k+1)} f(z)\\0 & 1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on $\Sigma$ has a unique solution given explicitly in terms of $p_{k+1}$, $p_k^*$ and Cauchy integrals against $f(s)\,ds/(2\pi i s^{k+1})$.
assumptions: $p_q$ are the orthonormal polynomials for the weight $f\,d\theta/(2\pi)$
conclusions: RHP has the unique solution $Y$ given in terms of $p_{k+1}, p_k^*$ and their Cauchy transforms

nodes.name: Properties of the $g$-function (Lemma 4.2)
nodes.statement: If $d\mu(\theta) = u(\theta)\,d\theta$ is an absolutely continuous probability measure on $\Sigma$ with $u(\theta) = u(-\theta)$, then $g(z) = \int_\Sigma \log(z-s)\,d\mu(s)$ has 8 listed properties: analytic in $\mathbb{C} - \Sigma \cup (-\infty,-1)$; $g_+(z) - g_-(z) = 2\pi i$ on $(-\infty,-1)$; $g(z) = \log z + O(1/z)$; $e^{qg}$ analytic in $\mathbb{C}-\Sigma$; $g(0) = \pi i$; $g_+ + g_- = 2\int \log|z-s|\,d\mu + i(\phi+\pi)$; $g_+ - g_- = 2\pi i \int_\phi^\pi d\mu$.

nodes.name: Equilibrium measure for $V = -\frac{\gamma}{2}(z+z^{-1})$ (Lemma 4.3)
nodes.statement: (i) If $0 \le \gamma \le 1$, then $d\mu_V(\theta) = \frac{1}{2\pi}(1 + \gamma\cos\theta)\,d\theta$ and $l = 0$. (ii) If $\gamma > 1$, then $d\mu_V(\theta) = \frac{\gamma}{\pi}\cos(\theta/2)\sqrt{1/\gamma - \sin^2(\theta/2)}\,\chi_{[-\theta_c,\theta_c]}(\theta)\,d\theta$ with $\sin^2(\theta_c/2) = 1/\gamma$ and $l = -\gamma + \log\gamma + 1$; the variational inequality is strict outside the support.
assumptions: External potential $V(z) = -\frac{\gamma}{2}(z+z^{-1})$ on the unit circle
conclusions: Explicit equilibrium measure and constant $l$ for $0 \le \gamma \le 1$
Explicit equilibrium measure with arc support and $l = -\gamma + \log\gamma + 1$ for $\gamma > 1$

nodes.name: Properties of $\alpha(z)$ for $\gamma > 1$ (Lemma 6.1)
nodes.statement: (i) $e^{2\alpha(z)}$ is independent of the path in $\mathbb{C} - (\overline{C_1} \cup \{0\})$. (ii) $\exp(-2\pi i \int_{\theta_c}^\phi d\mu_V(\theta)) = e^{2\alpha(z)}$ for $z = e^{i\phi}$, $|\phi| < \theta_c$. (iii) $\exp(2\int\log|z-e^{i\theta}|\,d\mu_V - V(z) + l) = e^{-2\alpha_-(z)}$ for $|\phi| > \theta_c$.
conclusions: Two integral identities relating $\alpha$ to the equilibrium-measure and variational data

nodes.name: Explicit solution of the $v^\infty$ RHP (Lemma 6.2)
nodes.statement: The RHP $(C_1, v^\infty)$ with $v^\infty = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on $C_1$ and $I$ off $C_1$ has the explicit solution $m^\infty = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\frac{1}{2}(\beta+\beta^{-1}) & \frac{1}{2i}(\beta-\beta^{-1})\\-\frac{1}{2i}(\beta-\beta^{-1}) & \frac{1}{2}(\beta+\beta^{-1})\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ where $\beta(z) = ((z-\xi)/(z-\xi^{-1}))^{1/4}$ analytic in $\mathbb{C} - \overline{C_1}$ with $\beta \to +1$ at $\infty$.
assumptions: Limit jump $v^\infty$ on the arc $C_1$ as $q \to \infty$

nodes.name: Asymptotics of $\kappa_{q-1}^2(\lambda)$ for $\gamma \le 1$ (Lemma 5.1)
assumptions: $\gamma$ in one of the three regimes (i)-(iii)
conclusions: Three regime-specific asymptotic bounds on $\kappa_{q-1}^2(\lambda)$ as $q \to \infty$

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|e^{-2\alpha}|$ in the gap regime (Lemma 6.3, $m^\infty$ inversion)
nodes.statement: For $\gamma > 1$, the explicit RHP $(C_1, v^\infty)$ admits the explicit solution $m^\infty$ with $m^\infty_{22}(0) = 1/\sqrt{\gamma}$, leading to the heuristic $\kappa_{q-1}^2 \sim e^{q(-\gamma + \log\gamma + 1)}/\sqrt{\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of $\kappa_{q-1}^2(\lambda)$ for $\gamma > 1$ (Lemma 6.4)
nodes.statement: As $q \to \infty$: (i) for $1 + \delta_3 \le \gamma$, $\kappa_{q-1}^2 = e^{q(-\gamma + \log\gamma + 1)} \frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}(1 + O(1/q))$; (ii) for $1 + M_3/(2^{1/3} q^{2/3}) \le \gamma \le 1 + \delta_4$, $\kappa_{q-1}^2 = e^{q(-\gamma + \log\gamma + 1)} \frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}(1 + O(1/(q(\gamma-1))))$; (iii) for $1 < \gamma \le 1 + M_4/(2^{1/3} q^{2/3})$, $|\kappa_{q-1}^2 - 1 - \frac{i 2^{4/3}}{q^{1/3}} m^{PII}_{1,22}(-t)| \le C(M_4)/q^{2/3}$ with $\gamma = 1 + t/(2^{1/3} q^{2/3})$.
assumptions: $\gamma$ in one of the three regimes (i)-(iii)
conclusions: Three regime-specific asymptotic bounds on $\kappa_{q-1}^2(\lambda)$ as $q \to \infty$ for $\gamma > 1$

nodes.name: Asymptotics of $\phi_n(\lambda)$ (Lemma 7.1)
nodes.statement: Set $t = 2^{1/3}(n+1)^{2/3}(1 - 2\sqrt{\lambda}/(n+1))$. Then 5 case-bounds on $\log\phi_n(\lambda)$: (i) bulk left tail $\le Ce^{-cn}$; (ii) intermediate left tail $\le Ce^{-c t^{3/2}}$; (iii) double-scaling regime $|\log\phi_n - \int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy| \le C(M_6)/n^{1/3} + Ce^{-M_6^{3/2}/4}$; (iv) intermediate right tail $\log\phi_n \le \frac{1}{96} t^3 + C(M_7)$; (v) bulk right tail $\phi_n \le Ce^{-C\lambda} \le Ce^{-cn^2}$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $q_{n,N}$ in $N$ (Lemma 8.1)
nodes.statement: For all $n, N \ge 1$, $q_{n,N+1} \le q_{n,N}$.

nodes.name: Tauberian de-Poissonization bound (Lemma 8.2)
nodes.statement: Let $m > 0$ fixed, $\mu_N^{(m)} = N + (2\sqrt{m+1}+1)\sqrt{N\log N}$ and $\nu_N^{(m)} = N - (2\sqrt{m+1}+1)\sqrt{N\log N}$. There exist $C(m), N_0(m)$ such that $\phi_n(\mu_N^{(m)}) - C/N^m \le q_{n,N} \le \phi_n(\nu_N^{(m)}) + C/N^m$ for $N \ge N_0$, $0 \le n \le N$.

nodes.name: De-Poissonization moment-bound (Lemma 8.3)
nodes.statement: There exists $C > 0$ such that $q_{n,N} \le C\,\phi_n(N - \sqrt{N})$ and $1 - q_{n,N} \le C(1 - \phi_n(N + \sqrt{N}))$ for all sufficiently large $N$ and $0 \le n \le N$.

nodes.name: Connection of RHP $Y$ to Toda lattice and Painlevé III
nodes.section: 3 Connection to the Toda Lattice and the Painlevé III Equation
nodes.statement: With $q = k+1$, the conjugated function $m^{TL}(z;q)$ satisfies a RHP that, on setting $\sqrt{\lambda} = t$ and $q = -2m$ for even $q$, coincides with the Toda-lattice RHP at reflection coefficient $r(z) \equiv 1$. Setting $\sqrt{\lambda} = -ix$ and conjugating gives the RHP for a particular Painlevé III equation with $\theta_\infty = -\theta_0 = q$.
conclusions: Equivalent RHP for Toda lattice with reflection coefficient $r \equiv 1$
Equivalent RHP for a specific PIII equation

nodes.name: Centering/scaling tail-bound for $F_N$
nodes.statement: For $M > 0$ sufficiently large, there exist $c, C(M) > 0$ with $F_N(t) \le C(M) e^{c t^3}$ for $-2N^{1/3} \le t \le -M$, and $1 - F_N(t) \le C(M) e^{-c t^{3/5}}$ for $M \le t \le N^{5/6} - 2N^{1/3}$.

nodes.name: Variational characterization of $d\mu_V$
nodes.statement: Euler-Lagrange conditions: there is $l \in \mathbb{R}$ with $2\int\log|z-s|\,d\mu_V(s) - V(z) + l = 0$ on $\overline{J}$ and $\le 0$ on $\Sigma - \overline{J}$, where $J = \mathrm{supp}(d\mu_V)$.

nodes.name: Identity $\frac{d}{dx} 2i m^{PII,1}_{1,22}(x) = u^2(x)$
nodes.statement: $\frac{d}{dx}\bigl(2i\, m^{PII,1}_{1,22}(x)\bigr) = u^2(x)$, with $2i\, m^{PII,1}_{1,22}(x)$ real-valued; this identity is what reduces $\int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy$ to $-\int_t^\infty (x-t) u^2(x)\,dx = \log F(t)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1 (RHP existence/uniqueness)
nodes.statement: Existence: direct check via Cauchy operator $C_+ - C_- = I$ that the candidate $Y$ satisfies the jump and asymptotics. Uniqueness: $\det Y = 1$ by Liouville, then $Z = Y\tilde{Y}^{-1}$ extends entire and tends to $I$ at infinity.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2 ($g$-function properties)
nodes.statement: Properties (i)-(v) are immediate from the definition of $g$. Property (vi) uses evenness of $u(\theta)$. Properties (vii) and (viii) are obtained by differentiating boundary-value integrals and identifying the constant via $F(\pi) = \pi$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3 (equilibrium measure)
nodes.statement: Case $0 \le \gamma \le 1$: explicit residue calculation for $g'(z)$ and the formula $g_+ + g_- = \log z - \frac{\gamma}{2}(z+z^{-1}) + \pi i$ verify the variational equality with $l = 0$. Case $\gamma > 1$: similar residue calculation on the gap-supported measure shows variational equality on $|\phi| \le \theta_c$ and strict inequality outside.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.1 ($\alpha$-properties)
nodes.statement: (i) Path-independence by residue calculation around $0$ (change $-\pi i$) and around $C_1$ (change $0$). (ii) Direct from definition of $\alpha$. (iii) Construct $F(\phi)$, show $F(\theta_c) = 0$ from variational condition and $F'(\phi) = 0$ via residue calculation; conclude $F \equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.3 (de-Poissonization moment bound)
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 8.1 to compare $\phi_n(N \pm \sqrt{N})$ with $q_{n,N}$: bound the Poisson sum by terms with $N' \in [N - \sqrt{N}, N]$ resp. $[N, N + \sqrt{N}]$, apply Stirling to the binomial-like factors, exploit monotonicity of the resulting exponent, and use $q_{n,N} \ge 0$ resp. $1 - q_{n,N} \le 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: Sandwich $F_N(t) = q_{n,N}$ between $\phi_n(\mu_N^{(m)}) \pm C/N^m$ via Lemma 8.2, push $N \to \infty$ then $M_6 \to \infty$ in Lemma 7.1 (iii), and identify the limit $\exp(\int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy) = F(t)$ via integration-by-parts using $\frac{d}{dx} 2i m^{PII}_{1,22} = u^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Express moments as integrals of $F_N$ and $1 - F_N$. Tail $t \le -M$: split $-2N^{1/3} \le t \le -2\delta N^{1/3}$ (use Lemma 7.1(v)) and $-2\delta N^{1/3} \le t \le -M$ (use Lemma 7.1(iv) with $\phi_n \le C(M) e^{c t^3}$); combine to get $F_N(t) \le C(M) e^{c t^3}$. Tail $t \ge M$: analogous split using Lemma 7.1(i) and Lemma 7.1(ii) yielding $1 - F_N(t) \le C e^{-c t^{3/5}}$. Apply dominated convergence using Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1 (case (ii) and (iii))
nodes.statement: Case (i) and (ii): factor $v^{(2)} = b_-^{-1} b_+$, deform onto $\Sigma^{(3)}$, use $\|w^{(3)}\|_\infty \le e^{-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} q (1-\gamma)^{3/2}}$ and $\|w^{(3)}\|_{L^1} \le C/q^{1/3}$ to bound $\kappa_{q-1}^2 - 1$. Case (iii): introduce a Painlevé II parametrix $m_p$ near $z = -1$ via $u = (z - z^{-1})/2$, $\lambda = q^{1/3} u/(i 2^{4/3})$. Show $\|v^{(3)} v_p^{-1} - I\|_\infty = O(1/q^{2/3})$ on $\mathcal{O}$ and exponentially small off $\mathcal{O}$; pass to $R = m^{(3)} m_p^{-1}$ and read off the $m^{PII}_{1,22}(t)$ correction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4 ($\gamma > 1$ asymptotics)
nodes.statement: Conjugate $m^{(2)}$ and use the factorization of $v^{(2)}$. Case (i): direct DKMVZ-type calculation gives $\kappa_{q-1}^2 = e^{q(-\gamma+\log\gamma+1)}/\sqrt{\gamma}(1+O(1/q))$. Case (ii): a finer analysis using $L^1$ bounds on $\|w_{\tilde{R}}\|$ gives the $1/(q(\gamma-1))$ error. Case (iii): introduce a PII parametrix using $m^{PII,3}$ via $u = (z - z^{-1})/(2i)$, $\lambda = q^{1/3} u / 2^{4/3}$, and use the relation $m^{PII}_{1,22} = m^{PII,3}_{1,22} + i x^2/8$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.1 ($\phi_n$ asymptotics)
nodes.statement: Use $\log\phi_n(\lambda) = \sum_{k \ge n} \log\kappa_k^2(\lambda)$ and split the sum into regimes determined by the value of $2\sqrt{\lambda}/(k+1)$. In each regime apply the corresponding bound from Lemma 5.1 or Lemma 6.4 (or Johansson's bound \eqref{e-J1.11} for the bulk right tail). Bound the resulting sums by integrals using monotonicity of the integrand, and identify the leading PII integral $\int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy$.

nodes.name: Numerical verification with Odlyzko-Rains constants $c_0, c_1$
nodes.statement: Solving Painlevé II numerically and computing $\int t^2\,dF - (\int t\,dF)^2$ and $\int t\,dF$ gives $0.8132$ and $-1.7711$, agreeing to two decimal places with the Monte Carlo constants $c_0 \sim 0.819$ and $c_1 \sim -1.758$ obtained for $\mathrm{Var}(l_N)/N^{1/3}$ and $(\mathbb{E}(l_N) - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6}$.

nodes.name: Length-3 increasing subsequences of $5\,1\,3\,2\,4$
nodes.statement: For $N = 5$ and $\pi = 5\,1\,3\,2\,4$ (one-line notation), the longest increasing subsequences are $1\,2\,4$ and $1\,3\,4$, so $l_5(\pi) = 3$.

nodes.name: Robinson-Schensted and second-row connection
nodes.statement: Under the Robinson-Schensted bijection $\pi \mapsto (P(\pi), Q(\pi))$, $l_N(\pi)$ equals the length of the first row. Monte Carlo of Odlyzko-Rains for the second-row length $\widetilde{l}_N$ matches the second-largest GUE eigenvalue: $\lim (\mathbb{E}_N(\widetilde{l}_N) - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6} = -3.618$, $\lim \mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{l}_N)/N^{1/3} = 0.545$.

nodes.name: Heuristic: Coulomb-gas interpretation in the Appendix
nodes.statement: Viewing $h_j = \mu_j + r - j$ as ``eigenvalues'' of a discrete $\beta = 2$ Coulomb gas on $\mathbb{Z}_+$ confined by an external potential, $\phi_n(\lambda) \approx P_{2\sqrt{\lambda}}(\lambda; n)$ becomes the analogue of the largest-eigenvalue distribution of a random Hermitian matrix, explaining the GUE link heuristically.

nodes.name: Phase transition at $\gamma = 1$
nodes.statement: The point $2\sqrt{\lambda}/(k+1) = 1$ corresponds to a third-order phase transition for the statistical system with partition function \eqref{e-DiS} (Gross-Witten 1980; Johansson 1998).

nodes.name: Ulam's problem
nodes.statement: Determine the limit $c \equiv \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E}_N(l_N)/\sqrt{N}$, and more generally the asymptotics of $q_{n,N} = \mathrm{Prob}(l_N \le n)$ as $N \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Variational problem for equilibrium measure
nodes.statement: Compute $E^V = \inf\{ I^V(\widetilde{\mu}) : \widetilde{\mu}$ probability measure on $\Sigma\}$, where $I^V(\widetilde{\mu}) = \iint \log|s-w|^{-1}\,d\widetilde{\mu}(s)\,d\widetilde{\mu}(w) + \int V(s)\,d\widetilde{\mu}(s)$ with $V(s) = -\sqrt{\lambda}(s + s^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Express $F_N(t)$ via $q_{n,N}$
nodes.statement: Set $n = [2\sqrt{N} + tN^{1/6}]$. Then $F_N(t) = \mathrm{Prob}((l_N - 2\sqrt{N})/N^{1/6} \le t) = q_{n,N}$.

nodes.name: Sandwich via de-Poissonization (Lemma 8.2)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 8.2 with $\mu_N^{(m)} = N + (2\sqrt{m+1}+1)\sqrt{N\log N}$, $\nu_N^{(m)} = N - (2\sqrt{m+1}+1)\sqrt{N\log N}$ to get $\phi_n(\mu_N^{(m)}) - C/N^m \le F_N(t) \le \phi_n(\nu_N^{(m)}) + C/N^m$.

nodes.name: Identify the rescaled parameter $t_N$
nodes.statement: Set $t_N = 2^{1/3}(n+1)^{2/3}(1 - 2\sqrt{\mu_N^{(m)}}/(n+1))$; then $2t \le t_N \le t/2$ for large $N$ and $t_N \to t$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7.1(iii) and double limit
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 7.1 (iii): $\phi_n(\mu_N^{(m)}) = \exp(\int_{t_N}^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy)(1 + O_{M_6}(n^{-1/3}) + O(e^{-M_6^{3/2}/4}))$. Take $N \to \infty$ then $M_6 \to \infty$ to get $\lim \phi_n(\mu_N^{(m)}) = \exp(\int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy)$. Same for $\nu_N^{(m)}$.

nodes.name: Convert to Tracy-Widom form via integration by parts
nodes.statement: Using $\frac{d}{dx} 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(x) = u^2(x)$ and integration by parts, $\exp(\int_t^\infty 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy) = \exp(-\int_t^\infty (x-t) u^2(x)\,dx) = F(t)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Reduce moments to integrals of $F_N, 1-F_N$
nodes.statement: Integration by parts: $\mathbb{E}_N(\chi_N^m) = -\int_{-\infty}^0 m t^{m-1} F_N(t)\,dt + \int_0^\infty m t^{m-1}(1 - F_N(t))\,dt$.

nodes.name: Left-tail bound $F_N(t) \le C(M) e^{c t^3}$
nodes.statement: For $t \le -M$: split $-2N^{1/3} \le t \le -2\delta N^{1/3}$ (apply Lemma 7.1(v) to get $\phi_n(N - \sqrt{N}) \le C e^{-cN} \le C e^{c t^3}$) and $-2\delta N^{1/3} \le t \le -M$ (apply Lemma 7.1(iv) using $-\gamma + \log\gamma + 1 \le -(\gamma - 1)^2/4$ to get $\phi_n(N - \sqrt{N}) \le C(M) e^{t^3/768}$). Combine via Lemma 8.3.

nodes.name: Right-tail bound $1 - F_N(t) \le C e^{-c t^{3/5}}$
nodes.statement: For $t \ge M$: split $2\delta N^{1/3} \le t \le N^{5/6} - 2N^{1/3}$ (apply Lemma 7.1(i) to get $1 - \phi_n(N + \sqrt{N}) \le C e^{-cn} \le C e^{-c t^{3/5}}$) and $M \le t \le 2\delta N^{1/3}$ (apply Lemma 7.1(ii) to get $1 - \phi_n \le C e^{-c t^{3/2}}$). Combine via Lemma 8.3.

nodes.name: Conclude via dominated convergence
nodes.statement: The pointwise convergence $F_N(t) \to F(t)$ from Theorem 1.1, together with the uniform tail bounds, gives by dominated convergence $\lim_N \mathbb{E}_N(\chi_N^m) = \mathbb{E}(\chi^m)$ for every $m \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Bulk left tail (case (i))
nodes.statement: If $0 \le 2\sqrt{\lambda}/(n+1) \le 1 - \delta_5$, then for any $k \ge n$, $2\sqrt{\lambda}/(k+1) \le 1 - \delta_5$. By Lemma 5.1(i), $|\log\phi_n(\lambda)| \le \sum_{k \ge n} C e^{-ck} \le C e^{-cn}$.

nodes.name: Intermediate left tail (case (ii)) via integral comparison
nodes.statement: Split $\sum_{k \ge n}$ into $n+1 \le k+1 \le 4\sqrt{\lambda}$ and $k+1 > 4\sqrt{\lambda}$. On the first range apply Lemma 5.1(ii); on the second Lemma 5.1(i). Bound the first sum by an integral exploiting monotonicity of $f(x) = e^{-(2\sqrt{2}/3) x (1-2\sqrt{\lambda}/x)^{3/2}}/x^{1/3}$ to get $\le C e^{-(n+1)(1 - 2\sqrt{\lambda}/(n+1))^{3/2}/2}$.

nodes.name: Double-scaling regime (case (iii)) via PII integral
nodes.statement: Split into three sub-ranges. On the central range use \eqref{e-z36} (combining Lemma 5.1(iii) and Lemma 6.4(iii)) to write each $\log\kappa_k^2$ in terms of $m^{PII}_{1,22}$, then convert the sum to an integral $\int_t^{M_6} 2i m^{PII}_{1,22}(y)\,dy$. The other ranges contribute $O(C(M_6)/n^{1/3} + e^{-M_6^{3/2}/4})$.

nodes.name: Intermediate right tail (case (iv))
nodes.statement: Split $\sum_{k}$ at $k+1 = 2\sqrt{\lambda} - M_7 (n+1)^{1/3}/2^{1/3}$. On the lower-$k$ range use the inequality $-\gamma + \log\gamma + 1 \le -(\gamma-1)^2/4$ together with \eqref{e-z37}; on the higher-$k$ range proceed as in cases (i)-(iii). Combine to get $\log\phi_n \le t^3/96 + C(M_7)$.

nodes.name: Bulk right tail (case (v)) via Johansson's bound
nodes.statement: For $1 + \delta_7 \le 2\sqrt{\lambda}/(n+1)$, invoke Johansson's bound \eqref{e-J1.11}: $\phi_n(\lambda) \le C e^{-C\lambda} \le C e^{-c n^2}$.

nodes.name: Set up the deformed RHP $m^{(3)}$ on $\Sigma^{(3)}$
nodes.statement: Use the equilibrium-measure $g$-function from Lemma 4.3(i) (with $l = 0$); conjugate to obtain RHP for $m^{(2)}$; factor $v^{(2)} = (b_-^{(2)})^{-1} b_+^{(2)}$ and deform onto a contour $\Sigma^{(3)}$ chosen along the steepest-descent paths of $\frac{\gamma}{2}(z - z^{-1}) + \log z$.

nodes.name: $L^\infty$ and $L^1$ bounds on $w^{(3)}$
nodes.statement: Show $\|w^{(3)}\|_\infty \le e^{-(2\sqrt{2}/3) q (1-\gamma)^{3/2}}$ from \eqref{e-sec2.13}-\eqref{e-sec2.15}, and $\|w^{(3)}\|_{L^1} \le C/q^{1/3}$ via splitting near $z = -1$ at angle $\widetilde{\theta} = q^{-1/3}\log q$.

nodes.name: Introduce PII parametrix near $z = -1$ for case (iii)
nodes.statement: Set $u = (z - z^{-1})/2$, $\lambda(z) = q^{1/3} u(z)/(i 2^{4/3})$, define $\Sigma^{PII,2} \cap \lambda(\mathcal{O}) = \lambda(\Sigma^{(3)} \cap \mathcal{O})$ and parametrix $m_p(z) = m^{PII,2}(\lambda(z), t)$ on $\mathcal{O}$, $m_p = I$ off $\mathcal{O}$.

nodes.name: Compare $v^{(3)}$ to $v_p$ and read off $m^{PII}_{1,22}(t)$
nodes.statement: Use Taylor expansion of $\log(\sqrt{1+u^2} - u) = -u + u^3/6 + u^5 r(u)$ to show $\|v^{(3)} v_p^{-1} - I\|_\infty \le C(M_2)/q^{2/3}$ on $\mathcal{O}$ and exponentially small off $\mathcal{O}$. Pass to $R = m^{(3)} m_p^{-1}$, evaluate $R_{22}(0)$ via the singular-integral solution formula, and obtain $\kappa_{q-1}^2 = 1 + (i 2^{4/3}/q^{1/3}) m^{PII,1}_{1,22}(t) + O_{M_2}(1/q^{2/3})$.
